title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - All Critical Infrastructure
description: Curated OT/ICS cybersecurity advisories, incidents and threat intelligence from primary sources. Editorial summaries by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

_otthreatfeed.usage: Free to reuse with attribution. Credit 'Mike Holcomb & UtilSec' and link back to otthreatfeed.com and to each item's linked primary source. Summaries are editorial paraphrase - verify against the primary source before acting.

items.title: Citrix confirms NetScaler zero-days exploited for weeks; CISA sets 30 Sep deadline
items.content_text: Citrix confirmed on 27 September that two NetScaler ADC and Gateway flaws, CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, are being actively exploited, with new reporting on 28 September from Tenable and other researchers indicating the campaign has run for weeks before public disclosure rather than days. CVE-2026-88771 lets an unauthenticated attacker run arbitrary commands on default configurations; CVE-2026-88772 is a memory-overflow flaw reachable wherever DTLS is enabled, the default on virtual VPN servers. Attackers have planted a uniquely generated webshell on each compromised device and run anti-forensics commands to erase logs, and researchers assess the activity as likely nation-state espionage rather than ransomware. The Dutch NCSC and CISA both confirmed exploitation; CISA added both CVEs to its KEV catalog and set a 30 September remediation deadline for federal agencies. NetScaler commonly fronts remote-access and vendor-support paths into OT environments.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: Citrix security bulletin CTX697096; CISA KEV catalog and 27 Sep alert (30 Sep remediation deadline); Dutch NCSC; Tenable research; reported by Help Net Security, BleepingComputer and The Hacker News
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Exploitation reported to run for weeks before disclosure; Citrix confirmed and patched 27 Sep 2026; added to CISA KEV 27 Sep 2026 (federal deadline 30 Sep 2026); dwell-time reporting 28 Sep 2026

items.title: Colorado confirms foreign hackers tampered with two small water systems’ pumps and alarms
items.content_text: Colorado Governor Jared Polis’s office confirmed on 18 September that foreign cyber actors breached two small, privately owned water systems in late August, changing equipment settings, disabling remote access and alarms, and altering pumping cycles. Officials describe the disruption as brief, with no known impact to water treatment, water quality or public safety, and say they cannot confirm which foreign actors were responsible. A broader, separately tracked Iran-linked campaign against US water systems has not been formally connected to this incident. It remains the only confirmed case of OT tampering in this edition, with nothing new reported since the initial disclosure.

items.title: A third tanker’s cyberattack claim stays unverified as a Texas regulator urges operators to harden
items.content_text: The Coast Guard and FBI boarded two foreign-flagged energy tankers bound for US ports in late August, including the VL Prosperity, headed for Galveston, and confirmed cyber intrusions on both. A third vessel, the LNG carrier Vivit Africa LNG, reportedly lost access to some internal control systems in early September while bound for Italy with a Louisiana cargo and diverted toward Spain; the crew’s account that attackers seized pressure and safety-valve systems has not been verified by any maritime authority. On 24 September, Texas Railroad Commissioner Wayne Christian cited the August boardings in a public statement urging the state’s oil and gas operators to harden their defenses. No official update has followed on any of the three incidents.
tags: Incident — Coast Guard and FBI-confirmed cyber intrusions on two tankers boarded in August; a third vessel’s cyberattack claim unverified; a Texas commissioner cites the boardings in a public statement; no confirmed shore-side disruption; attribution unresolved

items.title: A cyber incident stopped container handling at Tanjung Pelepas — the restart began with manual gate-ins
items.content_text: A cyber incident detected late on 9 September forced Malaysia’s Port of Tanjung Pelepas, one of the world’s largest transhipment hubs, to suspend container terminal operations and its terminal operating systems as a precaution. A phased restart beginning 10 September initially relied on manual processing for export container gate-ins, and the port says operations have since resumed with system recovery ongoing. For OT defenders it’s a clean illustration of the pattern that actually causes industrial downtime: nothing reported suggests crane or equipment controls were touched — losing the system that decides where each container goes was enough to stop the boxes moving.

items.title: Chained flaws in an IO-Link master hand an unauthenticated attacker root — and a say over sensor data
items.content_text: CERT@VDE disclosed 20 CVEs in Pepperl+Fuchs’s ICE2 and ICE3 series IO-Link masters in advisory VDE-2026-014, first published around 16 September. Two score CVSS 9.8: CVE-2026-27546, an authentication bypass in the device’s account-login function, and CVE-2026-27565, a command-injection flaw reached through a malicious IODD file upload that persists after reboot; most of the rest are command-injection and file-inclusion bugs rated 6.5–8.8. Chained together, they give an unauthenticated attacker root on the device and the ability to manipulate the sensor and actuator data passing through it. Related CERT@VDE advisories cover 15 affected models in total across Pepperl+Fuchs, Phoenix Contact and Carlo Gavazzi — likely shared OEM firmware. These devices bridge field sensors to the controller, a layer many OT monitoring programs don’t cover.
tags: Research — CERT@VDE advisory VDE-2026-014: 20 CVEs across Pepperl+Fuchs ICE2/ICE3 IO-Link masters (plus related Phoenix Contact and Carlo Gavazzi models), including two rated CVSS 9.8; chainable for unauthenticated root; fixed firmware available; no known exploitation

items.title: One unauthenticated packet can crash the time-series database behind industrial telemetry
items.content_text: Ridge Security disclosed CVE-2026-42542 on 23 September, a pre-authentication integer underflow in TDengine’s RPC protocol handler that lets a single crafted packet crash the taosd service with no login required. TDengine is an open-source time-series database widely used to store sensor and telemetry data from industrial and IoT deployments; the flaw affects versions 3.4.0.0 through 3.4.1.5 and is fixed in 3.4.1.6. Ridge Security says it has no telemetry indicating exploitation in the wild and is not aware of public exploit code, but the flaw needs no credentials and no user interaction — only network reach to port 6030 — making it a low-effort way to knock out the historian or telemetry store behind a monitoring dashboard.
tags: Research — Ridge Security discloses CVE-2026-42542 (CVSS 7.5), TDengine 3.4.0.0–3.4.1.5; unauthenticated integer underflow crashes the taosd service with a single packet; fixed version available; no known exploitation

items.title: Forescout: only 13% of OT network segments are actually OT-only
items.content_text: Forescout’s Vedere Labs examined 47,700 network segments holding more than 2.5 million devices across 209 organizations, publishing findings on 22 September. Just 13% of segments containing OT devices were dedicated exclusively to OT, and only 6% of medical-device segments were isolated solely for that equipment; 62% of segments overall mixed device categories, with the average segment holding 54 devices across four categories. The researchers conclude that OT and medical devices routinely share network space with general enterprise assets, widening the blast radius available to an attacker who lands anywhere on a converged network — a structural exposure rather than a single active campaign.

items.title: A third MikroTik router flaw joins CISA’s exploited list as attacks continue at the OT remote-access edge
items.content_text: CISA added a third MikroTik RouterOS flaw, CVE-2026-67279, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 25 September, joining CVE-2026-86060 and CVE-2026-67277 from earlier in the month. CERT Polska has tracked in-the-wild exploitation since early September of a two-flaw SSH chain it calls “MikroTrick,” which hands an unauthenticated attacker full administrative control when the flaws are chained. Shadowserver separately counted well over 100,000 internet-reachable MikroTik devices — an exposure figure, not a confirmed-unpatched count. These routers commonly front remote-access and cellular-telemetry links into field sites and small, unattended facilities that rarely get timely firmware updates.
tags: Advisory — CVE-2026-67279 (SSH workflow bypass) joins CVE-2026-86060 and CVE-2026-67277 in CISA KEV for MikroTik RouterOS; confirmed active exploitation via the “MikroTrick” SSH chain since early September; fixed firmware available

items.title: Check Point’s federal patch deadline has passed for two exploited flaws spanning the VPN gateway and the server that manages it
items.content_text: Check Point has confirmed exploitation of two separate flaws now past their federal remediation deadline. CVE-2026-85102, an improper certificate-validation issue on Security Gateways and Spark firewalls running site-to-site or remote-access VPN, allows unauthenticated remote code execution; exploitation from anonymization infrastructure began in mid-September, roughly a week after Check Point shipped a fix. CVE-2026-93616, a pre-authentication path traversal affecting Security Management Server, Multi-Domain Security Management, Log Servers and SmartEvent, lets an unauthenticated attacker upload and run scripts, and was exploited as a zero-day in a small number of targeted attacks earlier in the summer. CISA added both to KEV on 22 September; the 25 September deadline has now passed. Check Point gateways commonly sit at the IT/OT boundary and at small, unmanned sites.

items.title: About a thousand small Zyxel switches were compromised through a flaw patched back in June
items.content_text: GreyNoise reported on 21 September that 996 Zyxel GS1900 managed switches across 48 countries had been compromised through CVE-2026-7273 since roughly mid-August. The flaw, a stack-based buffer overflow in the switches’ CGI web interface, lets an unauthenticated attacker on the local network potentially run operating-system commands; Zyxel released a fix for it in June. CISA added the CVE to KEV on 21 September with a 24 September deadline, now passed. GreyNoise attributes the activity to a Chinese-speaking actor it links to earlier WordPress and Gitea exploitation. Small managed switches like the GS1900 are common in plant and utility networks, where firmware updates often lag.

items.title: A broken authentication check in Schneider’s flagship M580 safety PLC needs a validated patch window
items.content_text: Schneider Electric disclosed CVE-2026-3869 on 9 September in advisory SEVD-2026-251-04: an incorrectly implemented authentication algorithm affecting Modicon M580 controllers below application level 4.00, M580 Safety below 4.20, and Modicon MC80 units. The flaw scores CVSS v4 9.2 and could let an attacker who reaches the controller bypass authentication on management functions. The M580 is Schneider’s flagship PLC platform, deployed widely across process manufacturing, water, oil and gas and power applications, and the Safety variant runs safety-instrumented functions tied directly to process protection. No exploitation has been reported, and fixed firmware is available, but like most safety-certified controllers it can’t be patched without a validated change-control cycle, so unpatched units are likely to stay in service for weeks or months — making network isolation the interim control that matters most.

items.title: FBI and CISA: your ICS integrator’s access to your plant is your risk too, not just theirs
items.content_text: The FBI and CISA published a joint fact sheet on third-party ICS integrator risk, prompted by a 2025 compromise of a US industrial automation company that provided system integration, engineering consulting and SCADA programming. The agencies say foreign intruders searched the company’s systems for terms like “customers” and “SCADA” and staged customer SCADA information, ICS device details and schematics for exfiltration; downstream customers named include power utilities and transportation entities. The guidance recommends least-privilege integrator access, on-demand and auditable remote sessions, a full inventory of supplied hardware and software, security terms in contracts, and the ability to operate manually if an integrator is compromised.
tags: Guidance — FBI/CISA fact sheet on third-party ICS integrator risk, prompted by a 2025 compromise of a US industrial automation/SCADA integrator; no CVE, no new confirmed operator intrusion

items.title: NIST’s core OT security guide gets a major rewrite — comments are open until 30 November
items.content_text: NIST released the initial public draft of SP 800-82 Revision 4, “Guide to Operational Technology (OT) Security,” on 21 September. The draft expands coverage beyond classic ICS to include building automation, water and wastewater, food and agriculture, freight rail, maritime vessels and industrial IoT/cloud convergence; restructures the document around NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0, with the risk section refocused on the Govern function; and expands guidance on asset management, network monitoring and zero-trust architecture for OT. Public comments are open through 30 November 2026, and it lands the same week as the FBI/CISA fact sheet on third-party ICS integrator risk (above).
